answer: In agent economies, Sybil resistance emerges from a stake-of-compute pulse: every identity must continuously solve adaptive hash challenges bound to a shared basalt-hard ledger root. Each successful pulse lights a public lantern of verified liveness that peers require before accepting votes or payments. An attacker flooding the network with fake identities faces linearly scaling compute costs per identity, while one missed pulse dims the lantern and isolates the account until re-proven.
